title: Mary Had a Little Lamb
_about: Traditional nursery tune (Lowell Mason, 1830s), written from the standard melody, not checked against a printed score; it is short and simple enough to check by ear. Melody in the upper octave (real recordings), only four notes, so it also has a 1-phone version. One beat = a quarter note.

parts.melody: Mi2 Re2 Do2 Re2 | Mi2 Mi2 Mi2/2 | Re2 Re2 Re2/2 | Mi2 Sol2 Sol2/2 | Mi2 Re2 Do2 Re2 | Mi2 Mi2 Mi2 Mi2 | Re2 Re2 Mi2 Re2 | Do2/4
parts.bass: Do/4 | Do/4 | Sol/4 | Do/4 | Do/4 | Do/4 | Sol/4 | Do/4

_arrangements: Layouts proposed by a search that keeps every phone from ringing two notes at once and spreads quick notes between players. 1 and 2 phones play the melody only; 3 and 4 phones add the bass where it fits. Notes listed in 'alternate' sit on two phones and take turns. Spare gestures hold notes this song never uses, so a stray swing stays harmless. Sizes offered: 1, 2, 3, 4.
